desc: Makes and sells biscuits, chocolate and snacks under Oreo, Cadbury and Milka brands in more than 150 countries.
markets: Sells in over 150 countries, with strong emerging-market growth in India, Brazil and Southeast Asia; continues snack acquisitions.
rationale: Global snack brands could use F1 for fan sampling, limited-edition launches and hospitality in the US, Europe and Asia races.

desc: Operates Latin America's largest e-commerce marketplace plus Mercado Pago payments and logistics across Argentina, Brazil, Mexico and other countries.
markets: Operates in 18 Latin American countries, led by Brazil, Argentina and Mexico; expanding fintech credit and logistics investment.
rationale: F1 races in Brazil, Mexico and the US reach MercadoLibre's core Latin American shoppers and could showcase Mercado Pago.

desc: Runs Ross Dress for Less and dd's Discounts off-price apparel and home goods stores across the United States.
markets: Over 2,000 US stores, with plans to keep opening locations; no international presence.
rationale: Domestic off-price retailer with little brand-led marketing; F1 value for its value-seeking shoppers is weak.

desc: Operates around 2,000 general merchandise and grocery stores in the United States, plus an online business and own-brand products.
markets: Almost entirely US stores; Canadian expansion ended in 2015 and no overseas expansion is planned.
rationale: Strong US brand but purely domestic; F1 would suit only limited US-race fan activations and own-brand launches.

desc: Produces Huggies, Kleenex, Cottonelle and Kotex tissue, diapers and personal-care products sold in about 175 countries.
markets: Sells in about 175 countries, with sizeable Latin America, Asia and Europe business; acquiring a majority of Kenvue.
rationale: Global household brands could use F1 for consumer reach, though the product fit is weak and spend is cautious.

desc: Australian conglomerate owning Bunnings hardware, Kmart, Officeworks and chemicals and healthcare businesses, mostly serving customers in Australia and New Zealand.
markets: Retail operations in Australia and New Zealand; Bunnings and Kmart NZ expansion; some chemicals and healthcare exposure in Asia.
rationale: Home-market brand exposure at the Melbourne Grand Prix and corporate hospitality could suit Bunnings and Kmart, though overseas reach is limited.

desc: Canada's largest food and pharmacy retailer, running Loblaws, No Frills and Shoppers Drug Mart stores plus President's Choice products.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal offers a national-reach activation for President's Choice, but the company has little international marketing need.

desc: Runs Circle K convenience and fuel stores across North America, Europe and Asia, serving customers in about 30 countries.
markets: Operates in about 30 countries; pursued a bid for Seven & i in 2024-25 before withdrawing; ongoing store and fuel acquisitions.
rationale: Circle K fuel and convenience brand could use F1 for fan promotions across North America and Europe, linked to EV charging.

desc: Operates the eBay online marketplace connecting buyers and sellers of used, collectible and new goods in many countries.
markets: Active in about 190 markets, with focus on collectibles, pre-owned luxury and automotive parts; recently acquired Depop in some markets.
rationale: Used car-parts and collectibles categories fit motorsport fans; F1 merchandise and memorabilia listings could showcase the marketplace worldwide.

desc: Produces dairy products, plant-based foods, bottled water and infant nutrition, including Activia, Evian, Alpro and Aptamil brands worldwide.
markets: Sells in over 120 markets with growth in China, Latin America and North America; recently acquired Kate Farms.
rationale: Evian and Activia could use F1 for global hydration and health positioning, but sport hospitality is not central.

desc: Operates Walmart de Mexico y Centroamérica, with Bodega Aurrera, Walmart Supercenter and Sam's Club stores in Mexico and Central America.
markets: Stores in Mexico and Central America; continued store openings and e-commerce growth.
rationale: Mexico City Grand Prix gives a large home-market consumer activation, though Walmex has little global ambition.

desc: India's largest consumer goods company, selling soap, detergents, tea, foods and personal-care brands such as Lux and Surf Excel.
markets: Sells nationwide across India; part of the Unilever group, with no separate overseas expansion plans.
rationale: India has no F1 race currently, so brand impact is weak and spending is directed at local media.

desc: Britain's largest grocer, operating Tesco supermarkets and Clubcard loyalty, plus stores in Ireland and Central Europe.
markets: Stores in the UK, Ireland and Central Europe; rebuilding profit and growing Clubcard and retail media.
rationale: British Grand Prix gives national exposure to its Clubcard and Finest lines, but there is no clear international goal.

desc: Operates over 1,600 Dollarama fixed-price discount stores across Canada and owns a majority of Latin America's Dollarcity.
markets: Stores across Canada, with Dollarcity in Colombia, El Salvador, Guatemala and Peru; targeting more locations.
rationale: A value retailer with little brand marketing; F1 would offer only limited returns, mainly via the Montreal race.

desc: America's largest traditional supermarket group, operating Kroger, Ralphs, Fred Meyer and other grocery banners and its own private-label brands.
markets: US supermarkets only; terminated its Albertsons merger in 2024 and now focuses on e-commerce and own brands.
rationale: Exclusively domestic grocer; F1 relevance is weak, aside from possible own-brand fan promotions at US races.

desc: World's largest meat processor, selling beef, pork, chicken and prepared foods including Seara, Friboi and Pilgrim's brands in many countries.
markets: Plants and customers across the Americas, Australia, Europe and Asia; listed in New York in 2025; focus on prepared foods.
rationale: Brazilian Grand Prix and US races could support Seara and Friboi brand building, but commodity meat limits F1 appeal.

desc: Makes Persil detergents, Schwarzkopf hair care and Loctite adhesives for consumers and industry in about 80 countries.
markets: Operates in about 80 countries; strong adhesives business in industry and automotive, with ongoing portfolio streamlining.
rationale: Loctite adhesives sell to automakers and Schwarzkopf to consumers; F1 could support both B2B hospitality and mass-market brand exposure.

desc: Distributes food and kitchen supplies to restaurants, hospitals, schools and hotels in the United States, Canada, the UK and Europe.
markets: Operations in the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, France and Latin America; growing international distribution through acquisitions.
rationale: B2B foodservice supplier could use F1 hospitality to entertain restaurant and hotel customers, though brand marketing is minimal.

desc: Runs Woolworths supermarkets, Big W and Petstock in Australia and New Zealand's Countdown (now Woolworths NZ) grocery chain.
markets: Stores in Australia and New Zealand; focusing on e-commerce, retail media and Petstock expansion.
rationale: Australian Grand Prix in Melbourne offers a home-market loyalty and brand activation, but no international case.

desc: Operates Albert Heijn, Delhaize, Giant and Food Lion supermarkets in Europe and the United States, with an online grocery business.
markets: Stores across the Netherlands, Belgium, Central Europe and the eastern United States; expanding e-commerce and local formats.
rationale: Dutch and Belgian Grand Prix ties could support Albert Heijn and Delhaize brand activations, though the transatlantic fit is limited.

desc: Makes Hershey's, Reese's and Kisses chocolate and confectionery, and snacks like Pirate's Booty, sold mainly in North America.
markets: Mainly US and Canada; growing in Mexico, Brazil and India; recently bought LesserEvil snacks.
rationale: Confectionery brands could use US races in Miami, Austin and Las Vegas for fan sampling and limited-edition packs.

desc: Operates 7-Eleven convenience stores worldwide through Seven & i Holdings, with Japanese supermarkets and financial services alongside.
markets: Over 85,000 stores in about 20 countries, mostly 7-Eleven; spun off supermarkets and rejected Couche-Tard's takeover approach.
rationale: 7-Eleven's global retail reach could use F1 for brand campaigns in the US, Japan and Asia, though fit is limited.

desc: Holding company controlling Loblaw, grocery and drugstore operator, and owner of Weston Foods and real-estate holdings.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: Holding structure with few independent marketing needs; any F1 relevance would come only through Loblaw's Canadian activity.
flags: holding / investment vehicle, not an operating brand

desc: Sells premium kitchenware and furniture through Williams Sonoma, Pottery Barn and West Elm stores and websites, mainly in America.
markets: US stores plus online and franchise stores in the Middle East, Asia and Australia; growing international franchise partners.
rationale: Affluent home-product customers and B2B design clients could be reached through F1 hospitality, though the company has little motorsport history.

desc: Makes Heinz ketchup, Kraft cheese, Oscar Mayer meats and other packaged foods sold in North America and international markets.
markets: Sells in about 40 countries; Heinz is its main global growth brand, particularly in Europe, Asia and Latin America; planning to split in two.
rationale: Heinz ketchup has a global footprint and could support F1 fan campaigns, though spend is limited.

desc: Operates over 20,000 Dollar General discount stores, mostly in rural America, selling basic groceries and household goods.
markets: US only, with expansion in Mexico announced; continues to open and remodel stores.
rationale: Rural, price-driven customer base is distant from F1; domestic discount operator with minimal sponsorship culture.

desc: Runs South Korea's largest e-commerce platform, with fast delivery, Rocket Wow membership, Coupang Eats and expanding Taiwan operations.
markets: Mainly South Korea, with Taiwan expansion and Coupang Eats; invests in logistics and international growth.
rationale: F1 could help the Rocket Wow membership gain brand awareness in Taiwan and Korea, though no race there.

desc: Produces Arm & Hammer, Oxiclean, Trojan and Batiste household and personal-care brands sold mainly in North America.
markets: Mostly US, with growth in international consumer markets; ongoing bolt-on brand acquisitions.
rationale: Trojan and Arm & Hammer car-care brands could try US race activations, though the company's marketing is mainly retail-focused.

desc: Operates over 2,900 Casey's convenience and fuel stores across the Midwest United States, with a prepared-food and pizza focus.
markets: US Midwest only; growing by acquisition, including Fikes stores in Texas.
rationale: Regional convenience chain with no international goals; F1 value is minimal.

desc: Runs Dollar Tree and Family Dollar discount variety stores in the United States and Canada selling items at low prices.
markets: US and Canada only; sold Family Dollar in 2025 and now focuses on Dollar Tree.
rationale: Value retailer with little brand marketing; F1 sponsorship is unlikely to be cost effective.

desc: Produces umami seasoning, frozen foods, amino acids and healthcare ingredients, selling to consumers and food manufacturers in about 35 countries.
markets: Operations in about 35 countries, especially Asia, Brazil and the US; expanding its amino-science and semiconductor-material businesses.
rationale: B2B ingredient business and the Japanese Grand Prix could help build global food-science brand credibility.

desc: Makes Lindt and Ghirardelli premium chocolate, selling through its own shops and retail across Europe, North America and Asia.
markets: Sells in about 150 countries, with ongoing growth in the US and Asia and new shop openings.
rationale: Premium chocolate fits F1 hospitality gifting and luxury positioning, particularly in Monaco, Switzerland and the US.

desc: Runs Avenue Supermarts' DMart chain of discount supermarkets selling groceries and home goods in India.
markets: India only, with continued store expansion and DMart Ready online grocery.
rationale: Indian discount grocer with no motorsport marketing culture; F1 has little relevance.

desc: Distributes food and supplies to restaurants, hotels, schools and healthcare facilities across the United States.
markets: US only; growing through foodservice acquisitions such as Chef'Store.
rationale: B2B foodservice distributor could use US-race hospitality to host restaurant customers, but brand marketing is limited.

desc: Japan's largest retail group, running Aeon supermarkets and malls plus banking and drugstores in Japan, China and Southeast Asia.
markets: Operates in Japan, China and ASEAN countries such as Malaysia, Vietnam and Indonesia; building out malls and new supermarkets abroad.
rationale: Aeon's Asian mall network and Japanese Grand Prix could provide a pan-Asian consumer branding opportunity.

desc: Sells consumer electronics and appliances through Best Buy stores and online across the United States and Canada.
markets: US and Canada; stores in Mexico closed; expanding marketplace and health technology.
rationale: Technology retailer might link F1 to gaming and electronics promotions, but is domestic and lacks a sponsorship history.

desc: Operates Coles supermarkets and Liquorland and First Choice liquor outlets, serving Australian households.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: Melbourne Grand Prix offers a home-market brand platform, but limited relevance beyond Australia.

desc: Produces chicken, beef, pork and prepared foods such as Tyson and Jimmy Dean products, mainly for US retailers.
markets: Mainly US, with exports to Asia and Latin America; some international operations in Brazil and Thailand.
rationale: Commodity protein producer with little consumer marketing in motorsport, so F1 value is weak.

desc: Makes hygiene and health products such as Tork tissue, TENA incontinence care and Libero diapers sold in about 150 countries.
markets: Sells in about 150 countries, with strong positions in Europe, Latin America and Asia; investing in emerging markets.
rationale: Tork professional hygiene serves B2B customers, so F1 hospitality could help; consumer brands have a weak fit.

desc: Owns Primark fashion retail, plus Twinings, Ovaltine, Allied Bakeries and sugar and agriculture businesses sold in many countries.
markets: Primark in Europe and US; planned separation of Primark from food business; Primark expanding in the US and central Europe.
rationale: Primark could use F1 for youth-focused awareness in the US and Europe, though the group has little sport history.

desc: Runs rural lifestyle retail stores selling animal feed, tools and farm and home supplies across the United States.
markets: US only; adding new stores and the Allivet pet pharmacy.
rationale: Rural domestic retailer with little connection to F1; weak sponsorship case.

desc: Makes Cheerios, Pillsbury, Häagen-Dazs, Nature Valley and Blue Buffalo food and pet products sold in more than 100 countries.
markets: Sells in over 100 countries; growing Häagen-Dazs and pet food internationally; focus on North America.
rationale: Global snack and ice-cream brands could use US races for family-oriented fan sampling and limited-edition launches.

desc: Supplies taste and nutrition ingredients, such as flavours and proactive-health products, to food, beverage and pharmaceutical customers worldwide.
markets: Operations in about 30 countries; growth in Asia, Africa and Latin America; ongoing bolt-on acquisitions.
rationale: B2B ingredient supplier could use F1 hospitality to meet global food and beverage customers, but has little consumer marketing.

desc: Distributes food and supplies to restaurants and convenience stores in the United States, including Vistar and Core-Mark.
markets: US only; acquisitions in convenience and foodservice distribution.
rationale: B2B distributor with minimal brand marketing; F1 hospitality is possible but not obvious.

desc: Operates Falabella department stores, Sodimac home improvement, Tottus supermarkets and Banco Falabella across Chile, Peru, Colombia and Mexico.
markets: Stores in Chile, Peru, Colombia, Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Mexico; investing in e-commerce and marketplace expansion.
rationale: Latin American retailer could use Brazil and Mexico races for regional brand building and Banco Falabella card promotion.

desc: Runs the Allegro online marketplace in Poland and Central Europe, plus Allegro Pay, Mall and Czech platforms.
markets: Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Croatia; expanding cross-border Allegro Smart delivery.
rationale: No Central European race of note; F1 would only support the Allegro brand awareness in regional markets.

desc: Makes Transformers, Nerf, Play-Doh and Monopoly toys and games and Wizards of the Coast Magic: The Gathering card games.
markets: Sells in about 100 countries, with Wizards of the Coast digital and film partnerships; shifting to gaming-focused growth.
rationale: Toy and game licensing could connect with F1's younger fans; rival Mattel is an F1 partner so category exclusivity may block.

desc: Operates Muji stores selling clothing, household goods and food under a minimalist unbranded concept in Japan and over 20 countries.
markets: Over 1,000 stores across Japan, China, Europe and North America, with expansion in India and Southeast Asia.
rationale: Design-led lifestyle brand has little motorsport connection; F1 has only limited relevance for its minimalist positioning.

desc: World's largest baking company, producing Bimbo, Marinela, Sara Lee and Thomas' bread and snacks in about 30 countries.
markets: Plants in about 30 countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia; growing in the US, Europe and Asia with acquisitions.
rationale: Mexico City and US races reach Bimbo's core markets, supporting brand sampling and family-oriented activations.

desc: Operates duty-free shops, including Hainan stores and airport outlets, for travellers in China, and has some overseas duty-free operations.
markets: Mostly Hainan and mainland airports; limited overseas duty-free expansion through acquisitions.
rationale: Chinese Grand Prix and travel-retail luxury shoppers offer an affluent audience, though the company advertises little internationally.

desc: Runs Don Quijote discount stores across Japan, Asia and the United States, selling groceries, electronics and tourist goods.
markets: Stores in Japan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Thailand, Taiwan and the US; continued store openings in Asia and the US.
rationale: Japanese Grand Prix and Asia's inbound tourist retail flow could be used for brand awareness, but no motorsport link exists.

desc: Sells furniture and home goods online through Wayfair, AllModern and Birch Lane in the US, Canada and Europe.
markets: US, Canada, UK and Germany; opening a few physical stores in the US and growing its professional customer business.
rationale: Online home retailer could use F1 for reach and brand awareness, but marketing spend is focused on performance advertising.

desc: Operates Metro, Super C and Food Basics grocery stores and Jean Coutu pharmacies in Quebec and Ontario.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: Quebec-based grocer could use the Montreal race to reach local consumers, but has no international goals.

desc: Makes Folgers and Dunkin' coffee, Jif peanut butter, Smucker's jams and Hostess snacks, sold mostly in North America.
markets: Mainly US and Canada, with some international coffee sales; selling Hostess and Uncrustables growth focus.
rationale: Coffee and snack brands could use US races for sampling, but the brand has little motorsport history.

desc: Makes Tempur-Pedic, Sealy and Stearns & Foster mattresses and owns the Mattress Firm retail chain in the United States.
markets: Sells in the US and many other countries via Tempur Sealy; Mattress Firm adds US retail reach.
rationale: Sleep and recovery positioning could suit driver-performance storytelling; F1 partner Eight Sleep shows category interest, but exclusivity is a risk.

desc: Operates BJ's Wholesale Club warehouse stores, selling groceries and household goods to members in the eastern United States.
markets: Over 250 clubs in about 20 eastern US states; adding new clubs each year.
rationale: Regional membership club has no international ambitions; F1 would not provide any marketing benefit.

desc: Operates Pingo Doce supermarkets in Portugal, Biedronka discount stores in Poland and Ara stores in Colombia.
markets: Stores in Portugal, Poland and Colombia; expanding Ara in Colombia and opening Biedronka stores.
rationale: Portuguese Grand Prix in Portimão could support Pingo Doce, though marketing is mostly domestic.

desc: Runs Five Below stores selling low-priced toys, games, tech accessories and party items to US teenagers and pre-teens.
markets: US only; adding about 150 new stores a year.
rationale: Teen-focused retailer could use F1 for youth appeal, but marketing is mostly social and domestic.

desc: Sells sporting goods, athletic apparel and footwear through Dick's, Golf Galaxy and Foot Locker stores and websites.
markets: US only; acquired Foot Locker in 2025, with international exposure.
rationale: Sporting-goods retailer can use US races to sell team and driver merchandise and hospitality for key brand partners.

desc: Makes Clorox bleach and disinfectants, Pine-Sol, Brita filters, Burt's Bees and Hidden Valley, selling mostly in North America.
markets: US-centric, with sales in Canada, Latin America and Australia; investing in digital transformation.
rationale: Household cleaning brand with little motorsport link, so F1 offers only limited fan exposure.

desc: Operates 7-Eleven convenience stores across Thailand and owns the Makro wholesale and Lotus's retail chains in Southeast Asia.
markets: Thailand, Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar via Makro; expansion of 7-Eleven stores in Thailand and its Southeast Asian wholesale business.
rationale: Thai consumers at the Singapore and Japan races can be reached, but the company is mostly domestic.

desc: Sells video games, consoles and collectibles through GameStop stores and online in the United States and Europe.
markets: Stores in the US, Canada, Australia and Europe; closing underperforming overseas markets and holding bitcoin and cash reserves.
rationale: Gamers overlap with F1 audiences, but the retailer's finances are shaky and marketing spend is low.

desc: Makes Lotus Biscoff caramelised biscuits, spread and Nakd snack bars, sold in about 70 countries.
markets: Biscoff is sold in about 70 countries; building US and Asian presence and expanding production capacity.
rationale: Belgian Grand Prix heritage and Biscoff's global fan base fit F1 for brand building in Europe and North America.

desc: Processes milk into cheese, butter and dairy ingredients, selling in Canada, the United States, Europe, Australia and Argentina.
markets: Operations in Canada, US, Australia, UK and Argentina; investing in US cheese capacity.
rationale: Dairy processor with little consumer brand marketing; F1 would have limited relevance beyond a Montreal-race activation.

desc: Makes McCormick and Frank's RedHot spices, seasonings and flavours for consumers and food manufacturers worldwide.
markets: Sells in about 150 countries; growing spices and flavour solutions in Asia and Europe.
rationale: B2B flavour solutions customers and food brands could use F1 for hospitality, though motorsport is not central.

desc: World's largest Atlantic salmon producer, farming and selling fresh and processed seafood to customers in about 70 countries.
markets: Sells in about 70 countries, with markets in Europe, North America and Asia; growing its consumer products division.
rationale: Seafood producer with limited consumer branding; F1 could provide a premium-hospitality angle but is not obvious.

desc: Makes Spam, Hormel Natural Choice, Planters and Jennie-O packaged meats and snacks, selling mainly in the United States.
markets: Mostly US, with some exports and international franchises; Planters nuts and Spam in Asia.
rationale: Packaged-food company with little motorsport marketing; F1 relevance is low.

desc: Makes biscuits, bread, cakes and dairy products such as Good Day and Marie Gold, sold in India and abroad.
markets: Sells across India and in about 80 countries, with exports to the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: India has no F1 race; Middle East race audiences could aid its export brands, but marketing fit is weak.

desc: Sells furniture and home goods through Nitori stores in Japan, Taiwan, China and the United States.
markets: Stores in Japan, Taiwan, China, South Korea and the US; targeting more overseas stores.
rationale: Furniture retailer with domestic marketing; F1 fit is weak despite expansion in Asia.

desc: Sells Magnum, Ben & Jerry's and Wall's ice cream in dozens of countries; spun off from Unilever in December 2025.
markets: Operations in about 60 countries across Europe, Asia and the Americas; independent listing since December 2025.
rationale: Ice cream fits hospitality and fan sampling at summer races; Magnum is a strong consumer brand to build globally.

desc: Produces dairy, juice, bakery and poultry products sold across Saudi Arabia, the Gulf, Egypt and Jordan.
markets: Saudi Arabia, GCC, Egypt, Jordan and the US; investing in poultry and dairy capacity in new markets.
rationale: Saudi, Qatar and Abu Dhabi races provide direct access to Almarai's Gulf consumers and a regional brand-building platform.

desc: Makes Shimano bicycle components, such as gears and brakes, and fishing tackle, selling to bike makers in over 100 countries.
markets: Sells in over 100 countries; Europe is its largest market; manufacturing in China, Malaysia and Indonesia.
rationale: Premium engineering brand with B2B ties to bike makers; F1 gives a technology showcase, but cycling is the core.

desc: Sells Tata Tea, Tetley, Tata Salt and Himalayan water, plus Starbucks India coffee, mainly in India.
markets: India, UK, US, Canada and Australia for tea; expanding its Soulfull and Tata Sampann brands.
rationale: Tetley tea has UK and US reach, so British and US races could help brand building, but Indian focus remains.

desc: Operates hypermarkets, supermarkets and convenience stores in France, Spain, Italy, Belgium, Brazil and Argentina, plus retail media and financial services.
markets: Stores in France, Spain, Italy, Belgium, Poland and Latin America; exiting Italy and Poland to focus on core markets.
rationale: French and Spanish Grand Prix link could support the Carrefour brand, but marketing is mostly retail-focused.

desc: Africa's largest supermarket group, operating Shoprite, Checkers and Usave stores in South Africa and Africa.
markets: South Africa, Namibia, Botswana, Zambia and Eswatini; exited other African countries and focuses on Checkers Sixty60 delivery.
rationale: South Africa has no F1 race at present, so a partnership would have little local activation value.

desc: World's largest pork company, operating Smithfield in the US, Shuanghui in China and European operations, selling packaged and fresh pork.
markets: US, China and Europe; Smithfield was listed in the US in 2025; building packaged foods.
rationale: Commodity pork producer with limited consumer branding; F1 relevance is low except for Chinese Grand Prix exposure.

desc: Operates K-Group grocery, building and technical trade stores in Finland, Sweden and the Baltic states.
markets: Finland, Sweden, Norway, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania; focusing on grocery and retail media.
rationale: Nordic domestic retailer without an F1 race nearby; sponsorship fit is poor.

desc: Makes branded food products such as Felix, Bubs, Abba and Lilleborg household goods for Nordic and Baltic consumers.
markets: Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Baltics and India for selected brands; bolt-on acquisitions in Nordic brands.
rationale: Nordic packaged-food group could use F1 for brand awareness, though there is no natural link.

desc: Britain's second-largest supermarket group, operating Sainsbury's, Argos and Habitat stores and the Nectar loyalty scheme.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: British Grand Prix sponsorship might help Nectar and Argos brands, but marketing is entirely UK-focused.

desc: Makes Kikkoman soy sauce and seasonings, sold in about 100 countries with production in Japan, the US and Asia.
markets: Sells in about 100 countries; US and Asian plants; steady export growth.
rationale: Global food brand might use F1 in the US and Japan for restaurant partnerships, but there is no obvious fit.

desc: Runs Ozon, one of Russia's largest online marketplaces, offering delivery, fintech services and its own logistics network.
markets: Russia and neighbouring CIS countries, including Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia and Uzbekistan.
rationale: F1 does not currently race in Russia and sanctions risk makes sponsorship essentially unfeasible.

desc: Operates over 2,500 Dino convenience supermarkets in small Polish towns selling food and household items.
markets: Poland only, with continuing store openings.
rationale: Domestic Polish grocer with a limited marketing culture; F1 has no clear role.

desc: Operates Dillard's department stores selling fashion and home goods in about 270 locations across the southern US.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: US department store with little brand marketing; F1 hospitality could suit its upscale shoppers but is unlikely.

desc: Makes Godrej household insecticides, soaps and hair colour for India, Indonesia, Africa and Latin America.
markets: India, Indonesia, Africa and Latin America; expanding Africa and Indonesia ranges.
rationale: Emerging-market consumer-goods maker with limited motorsport link; F1 offers weak reach.

desc: Operates BIM discount stores across Turkey, Morocco and Egypt selling limited-range groceries and private-label goods.
markets: Turkey, Morocco and Egypt; continuing store openings.
rationale: Turkish discount grocer with no brand-marketing culture; F1 relevance is weak.

desc: Sells pet food, medications and supplies through the Chewy online store with autoship and pet-care clinics across the US.
markets: US only, with Canada expansion; opening Chewy Vet Care clinics.
rationale: Online pet retailer has limited motorsport overlap; F1 offers only US fan exposure.

desc: Operates Rakuten Ichiba online marketplace, Rakuten Card, Rakuten Mobile and Viber messaging, selling services in Japan and abroad.
markets: Japan-centred, with Viber global; Rakuten Mobile expansion; earlier Barcelona and Golden State Warriors sponsorships.
rationale: Rakuten has sponsored global sport; F1 could showcase marketplace and mobile services to Japanese and international users.

desc: Licenses and sells Hello Kitty and other character goods and operates theme parks, selling in Japan and about 130 countries.
markets: Sells in about 130 countries; growth in the US, China and Southeast Asia; expanding licensing.
rationale: Character brands can attract young fans; F1 collaborations and collectibles could expand its licensing in Asia and the US.

desc: Produces farmed Atlantic salmon in Norway and Iceland and sells seafood worldwide, with offshore farming projects.
markets: Exports to Europe, Asia and the US; developing offshore farms and value-added products.
rationale: Salmon exporter with little consumer branding; F1 hospitality in Norway is a limited platform.

desc: Operates Tiendas 3B discount stores in Mexico selling basic groceries and private-label goods.
markets: Mexico only; opening hundreds of stores a year.
rationale: Mexico City Grand Prix could raise discount-brand awareness, but it is a domestic budget retailer.

desc: World's largest cocoa and chocolate maker, supplying chocolate and cocoa products to food manufacturers and chocolatiers worldwide.
markets: Plants in about 30 countries; customers include global confectioners; focus on Asia and Latin America.
rationale: B2B ingredient supplier could use F1 hospitality for key confectionery customers, but there is little consumer brand to promote.

desc: Runs duty-free shops and restaurants in airports, motorway stops and cruise ports in over 70 countries, formerly Dufry.
markets: Stores in about 70 countries, with growth in the Americas, Middle East and Asia.
rationale: Airport retail and F1 travel audience overlap, giving a venue for luxury and hospitality offers.

desc: Operates Canadian Tire, Mark's and SportChek stores selling automotive, sports, leisure and home goods across Canada.
markets: Canada only, with a retail financial services arm.
rationale: Automotive parts and sports lines suit the Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal as a national marketing platform.

desc: Operates Sobeys, Safeway and FreshCo grocery stores across Canada and holds real-estate assets.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: Canadian grocer without international plans; F1 offers little commercial benefit.

desc: Operates over 11,000 Żabka convenience stores in Poland and Romania, with the Żappka app and Jush stores.
markets: Poland and Romania; opening stores in Romania and growing the autonomous Jush format.
rationale: Convenience chain with local brand focus; F1 relevance is limited.

desc: Runs Naukri job portal, 99acres property and Jeevansathi matrimony websites in India and also invests in start-ups.
markets: India only; Naukri has some Gulf presence; invests in Zomato and other start-ups.
rationale: Job-portal brand with Indian focus; F1 has little relevance for its audience.

desc: Runs B&Q, Screwfix and Castorama home-improvement stores in the UK, France and Poland.
markets: UK, France, Poland and Romania; focusing on Screwfix growth and closing weaker stores.
rationale: Trade customers could be hosted at the British Grand Prix, but Kingfisher has not used global sports sponsorship.

desc: Operates Isetan and Mitsukoshi department stores in Japan and has international outlets in Asia and Europe.
markets: Stores in Japan, Singapore, Malaysia, China and Europe; tapping inbound tourist demand.
rationale: Luxury shoppers align with F1 hospitality, and the Japanese Grand Prix is local, but no sports sponsorship record exists.

desc: Operates the Zalando online fashion platform selling clothing and shoes in about 25 European countries.
markets: Operates in around 25 European countries; integrating About You acquisition; expanding partner programme.
rationale: Fashion e-commerce could use F1 for youth reach across Europe, with Grand Prix fashion tie-ins.

desc: Makes frozen potato products such as french fries sold to restaurants and retailers in over 100 countries.
markets: Sells in over 100 countries; plants in North America, Europe and China; growing in Asia and Latin America.
rationale: B2B supplier to restaurant chains could use F1 hospitality, though it has no consumer brand to promote.

desc: Runs Etsy, Reverb and Depop online marketplaces for handmade, vintage and unique goods sold in many countries.
markets: Buyers and sellers in about 230 countries; focus on US, UK, Germany and France.
rationale: Creative marketplace could use F1 for global reach, but brand fit with motorsport is weak.

desc: Makes Meiji chocolate, dairy, yoghurt, infant formula and pharmaceuticals, selling mostly in Japan with operations in Asia and the US.
markets: Japan, China, Southeast Asia and the US; expanding nutrition products in Asia.
rationale: Japanese Grand Prix could help Meiji's consumer brands, but its international ambitions are limited.

desc: Runs the Monotaro online platform selling industrial supplies and tools to factories and workshops in Japan and abroad.
markets: Japan, with subsidiaries in Korea, Indonesia, India and Vietnam.
rationale: B2B industrial e-commerce site could use F1 hospitality to meet customers, but has no brand marketing tradition.

desc: Produces fresh pork, bacon and packaged meats including Smithfield and Eckrich brands, selling mainly in the United States.
markets: US-centred, with sales in Europe and Asia through WH Group; raised funds in its 2025 US listing.
rationale: Packaged-meat brand could use US-race promotions, but F1 value is limited.

desc: Designs and sells Warhammer miniature wargames, paints and books through its own stores and trade partners worldwide.
markets: Sells in many countries; stores in the UK, US, Canada and Australia; strong licensing, including Amazon Prime's Warhammer series.
rationale: Hobby brand has strong licensing; F1 audiences overlap with gamers and collectors, but sponsorship is not a typical play.

desc: Farmer-owned dairy co-operative collecting milk and exporting milk powder, cheese, butter and ingredients to customers in over 100 countries.
markets: Exports to over 100 countries, with major business in China, Southeast Asia and the Middle East; selling consumer business.
rationale: B2B dairy supplier could use F1 hospitality for foodservice clients in Asia, but consumer brand use is limited.
flags: holding / investment vehicle, not an operating brand

desc: Operates Pepco, Dealz and Poundland variety discount stores in Central and Eastern Europe and the UK.
markets: Poland, Central and Eastern Europe, Italy and the UK; Poundland restructuring and store growth in Europe.
rationale: Value retailer with limited marketing; F1 is unlikely to deliver value.

desc: Makes Birds Eye, Banquet, Slim Jim and Marie Callender's frozen and packaged foods, mostly sold in the United States.
markets: Mainly US, with small Canadian and international sales.
rationale: Packaged-food firm with little motorsport marketing; F1 relevance is weak.

desc: Operates Taiwan's 7-Eleven convenience stores along with Starbucks Taiwan and Cold Stone outlets, and operates in the Philippines.
markets: Taiwan, the Philippines and China; building retail logistics and new store formats.
rationale: Domestic convenience operator with limited motorsport relevance; F1 could still raise brand awareness through its Starbucks and 7-Eleven partners.

desc: Makes Campbell's soup, Goldfish crackers, Pepperidge Farm and Snyder's-Lance snacks sold mostly in North America.
markets: US-led with sales in Canada and Australia; acquired Sovos Brands.
rationale: Snack brands could use US races for sampling, but sponsorship is not part of its strategy.

desc: Produces chicken for retail and foodservice customers in the United States, Mexico and the UK and Europe.
markets: US, Mexico and Europe; JBS holds majority stake.
rationale: Commodity poultry producer with little brand marketing; F1 offers weak value.

desc: Operates Macy's, Bloomingdale's and Bluemercury department stores and beauty shops in the United States.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: US department store could use US races for fashion and beauty promotions, but spending is constrained.

desc: Runs ZOZOTOWN, Japan's largest online fashion marketplace, and the ZOZO try-on and private-brand businesses.
markets: Mainly Japan, with limited overseas ZOZOTOWN reach.
rationale: Japanese fashion shoppers overlap with Japanese Grand Prix fans, but sponsorship would be niche.

desc: Makes Maruchan instant noodles and seafood products, selling in Japan, North America and Mexico.
markets: Japan, the US, Mexico and Asia; expanding North American noodle production.
rationale: Maruchan is a recognised US instant-noodle brand; F1 US races could build its young audience.

desc: Produces milk products, cheese and yoghurt such as Emmi Caffè Latte, mainly in Switzerland and in 15 other countries.
markets: Switzerland, the US, Spain, Chile and other countries; expansion through acquisitions of niche dairy brands.
rationale: Swiss dairy group might use the F1 platform for Caffè Latte, but the case is weak.

desc: Operates Vipshop, a Chinese online discount retailer selling branded apparel, cosmetics and household goods through flash sales.
markets: China only.
rationale: Chinese e-commerce firm with no overseas market; F1 value is mostly domestic brand awareness at the Shanghai race.

desc: Operates 99 Speed Mart convenience stores across Malaysia selling groceries and daily necessities.
markets: Malaysia only, with plans to open new stores.
rationale: Domestic Malaysian convenience chain; F1 would be too costly for its marketing needs.

desc: Operates Willys, Hemköp and Axfood Snabbgross grocery stores and wholesale in Sweden.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: Swedish grocer with no international business; F1 sponsorship offers little commercial value.

desc: Makes and sells diapers, tissues, feminine care and Kleenex products in Mexico and Central America.
markets: Mexico and Central America; Kimberly-Clark Corporation is a major shareholder.
rationale: Mexican Grand Prix could support brands like Huggies, but Kimberly-Clark's global strategy limits local sponsorship.

desc: Operates Albertsons, Safeway and Vons supermarkets and pharmacies across the United States.
markets: No verified expansion plans
rationale: US grocery chain with minimal brand marketing; F1 sponsorship would have little relevance.
